subject: zoology_2
question_text: How many amino acids and polypeptide chains are present in insulin?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.60, VSAQ 144. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The total
steps.why: The two chains together make up the whole hormone, so their lengths add to the total.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the number of chains.
lines: 51 amino acids are present in insulin.
They are arranged in two polypeptide chains.

steps.label: The two chains
steps.why: Chain A is the shorter of the two, and the difference in length is worth remembering.
lines: 21 amino acids form polypeptide chain A.

lines.text: 30 amino acids form polypeptide chain B

insider_note: Three numbers, and all three are marked: 51 in total, 21 in chain A, 30 in chain B.
